newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen flat-off $0.50-dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen flat-off $0.50-dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Tuesday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt lower, pressured by increased hog marketings, livestock dealers said.
Marketings late last week were largely frozen by blowing snow, bitterly cold weather and dangerous wind chill readings.
Subsiding winds and slightly warmer weather on Monday released more hogs on the market, with even greater numbers expected Tuesday as temperatures moderate further, they said.
Top prices for hogs delivered to interior Iowa and southern Minnesota plants were seen ranging from $54.00 to $54.50 and Illinois tops at the plant could span $53.50-$54.00.
Indiana/Ohio top prices for hogs at the plant were seen ranging from $52.50 to $53.00, sources there said.
Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hog receipts Monday were estimated at 115,000 head, according to USDA. Friday's interior movement was 39,000 head, compared with that day's estimate of 60,000.
About 150,000 to 200,000 hogs were backed up by last week's weather, said Dale Benson, livestock analyst with Dean-Witter Reynolds in Chicago.
"The question is: Will producers be able to move them before a new storm moves in at midweek?," Benson said.

A new storm was expected to move into the western Corn Belt from the central Plains Tuesday, followed by another round of low temperatures. The storm could produce light to moderate snowfall and strong winds, forecasters said.
